source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: Supports for Students with Disabilities (Saskatchewan Student Aid)
entries.description: Saskatchewan Student Aid's supports for post-secondary students with a permanent, persistent or prolonged disability. Along with regular student loans and grants, students may get the Canada Student Grant for Students with Disabilities and the Canada-Saskatchewan Grant for Services and Equipment for Students with Disabilities. They can apply for student aid with a reduced course load (40% to 59% of a full load) and are not required to make a fixed contribution to their education costs.
entries.cost_note: Loans and grants for students; the page does not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: There are many supports available to assist students with permanent, persistent or prolonged disabilities in accessing and succeeding in their post-secondary studies.
entries.notes: CNAF's four student-aid links (Student Service Centre Post Secondary, Student Loan Application, Canada and Saskatchewan Student Grants, and the Grant for Services and Equipment form) all go to old saskatchewan.ca paths that now return 'Page Not Found'; the program's current page is under saskatchewan.ca/residents/education-and-learning/saskatchewan-student-aid. Phone is for Student and Support Services; the page's email is hidden by the site, so it is left out. Covers the 2026-27 year; graduates with disabilities may also use the Repayment Assistance Plan for Borrowers with Disabilities (RAP-D).

entries.name: Saskatchewan Human Rights Commission
entries.description: The provincial agency that works to discourage and eliminate discrimination under the Saskatchewan Human Rights Code. People who believe they have been discriminated against can file a complaint online with the Intake Questionnaire, by mail, or with help by phone. The Commission also publishes education resources and runs systemic initiatives, including one on students with intensive needs.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention any fee for filing a complaint.
entries.evidence: If you believe you have experienced discrimination, you can file a complaint with the Saskatchewan Human Rights Commission in several ways.
entries.notes: CNAF links to gov.sk.ca/shrc pages (and a qp.gov.sk.ca copy of the Code); that domain no longer resolves. The Commission now uses saskhrc.ca (saskatchewanhumanrights.ca redirects there). Contact details from the site footer (toll free 1-800-667-9249); the only address shown is P.O. Box 6011, Saskatoon SK S7K 4E4, so address is left null. CNAF's second listing, 'Human Rights Protections for Students with Disabilities', is a page of this Commission.

entries.name: Autism Services of Saskatoon
entries.description: A Saskatoon charity serving autistic children, youth and adults, from age 2, and their families. Its programs include the ABA Little Tots program for children 48 months or younger, an Autism Intervention Program, group homes and day programs, family recreation programs, a mental health and wellness team (in person and virtual) and employment supports. Services start with the agency intake process, and adults over 19 can ask about autism assessments.
entries.cost_note: The pages checked do not mention program fees.
entries.evidence: Autism Services is a Saskatoon-based, charitable organization dedicated to providing advocacy, support, education, recreational, and social and residential programs and services to individuals with autism spectrum disorder and their families.
entries.notes: CNAF links to autismservices.ca/about-us/, which now returns 404; the About page is at /about/. Programs from the Programs & Services page; address, phone and email from the Contact page. Recent news posts are dated September and October 2026. CNAF describes it only as running three homes for adults; it now offers a much wider range of services.

entries.name: Prince Albert Group Homes Society (PAGHS)
entries.description: A Prince Albert charity, started by parents in 1973, that runs 12 group homes and individual day programs for adults with intellectual and other developmental disabilities, including autistic adults. Each home is shared with 1 to 5 other people and has 24-hour support staff, and residents can take part in community day programs; it also supports people living independently.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost; it says its main funder is the Ministry of Social Services through Community Living Service Delivery (CLSD).
entries.address: 203 – 31st Street East Prince Albert, SK S6V 8A8
entries.evidence: Prince Albert Group Homes Society manages 12 homes in our mission to provide adults with intellectual disabilities person-centered support, care and services that improve their quality of life
entries.notes: CNAF links to paghs.ca/programs.php, which now returns 404; the site's current pages are Who We Are, Our Homes and Let's Talk (contact). Address and phone are for the main office.

entries.name: Community Living Service Delivery (CLSD)
entries.description: A branch of Saskatchewan's Ministry of Social Services that helps people with intellectual disabilities get community-based services. Each eligible person is assigned a Community Services Worker, and CLSD connects people with housing (approved private service homes, group homes, group living homes, supported living) and day programs, with a self-directed funding option for adults. People apply through the nearest Community Living Service Delivery office.
entries.cost_note: The page does not list fees; people in group living homes pay basic shelter costs, and funding is given by urgency and priority of need.
entries.evidence: Community Living Service Delivery (CLSD) is a branch of the Ministry of Social Services that works with people with intellectual disabilities and helps them access a variety of community-based services.
entries.notes: CNAF's two links ('Community Living' and 'Community Living Website') both point to a 2011 PDF on a school-division blog (blogs.gssd.ca) that timed out; the program's current page is on saskatchewan.ca. No single phone number: the page links to a list of local offices. Community Services Workers also offer family support such as counselling and respite planning.

entries.name: Alvin Buckwold Child Development Program (ABCDP)
entries.description: A Saskatchewan Health Authority child development program at the Kinsmen Children's Centre in Saskatoon, part of the SHA's Maternal and Children's Provincial Program. Families can contact it by phone or through its intake email.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Alvin Buckwold Child Development Program (ABCDP) is located at the Kinsmen Children’s Center in Saskatoon and is a part of the Saskatchewan Health Authority’s Maternal and Children’s Provincial Program.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old Saskatoon Health Region site, which now redirects to the Saskatchewan Health Authority home page; the program has a facility page on saskhealthauthority.ca. That page gives only the location and contacts; it does not describe services or ages (CNAF says it offers assessment, diagnosis, therapy and medical services for children and youth), so a reviewer may want to confirm before adding tags.

entries.name: Saskatchewan CEC (Council for Exceptional Children, Saskatchewan Unit)
entries.description: The Saskatchewan unit of the Council for Exceptional Children, an international community of educators in special and gifted education. It gives Yes I Can! awards to students in grades 4 to 12 who receive intensive supports and Harry Dahl scholarships and awards, and holds an annual general meeting.
entries.cost_note: Membership is through CEC (the site links to CEC's join/renew page); no fees are listed.
entries.evidence: These award acknowledges the achievements of children and youth with intensive supports (grades 4-12) who have overcome challenges or public misconceptions.
entries.notes: The site looks stale: the latest dated items are from 2019 and 2020, it lists no upcoming events, and its Contact page gives only the US-based CEC membership team's numbers (888/232-7733), so phone is left null. It is an association for special educators rather than a direct service for families; a reviewer may prefer to drop it.
